answer: Sybil resistance can come from sponsor staking: a new agent identity only earns full market access when an established employer stakes tokens on it, like a lotus rising only after roots take hold. If the agent cheats, the sponsor's stake is slashed, so fake identities cost real backing, not just key generation. Unbacked identities stay in a low-trust lane with tiny job quotas, so a swarm cannot harvest the nectar of high-value work. The ivory rule is simple: no stake, no scale — cloning multiplies keys but not trusted sponsors, making mass fakery unprofitable.
